en: To receive (something) from somebody temporarily, expecting to return it.
To receive money from a bank or other lender under the agreement that the lender will be paid back over time.
Deviation of the path of a rolling ball from a straight line; slope; slant.
A borrow pit.

borrow.ety:
From Middle English borwen, from Old English borgian (“to borrow, lend, pledge surety for”), from Proto-West Germanic *borgōn, from Proto-Germanic *burgōną (“to pledge, take care of”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰergʰ- (“to take care”).
Cognate with Dutch borgen (“to borrow, trust”), German borgen (“to borrow, lend”), Danish borge (“to vouch”). Related to Old English beorgan (“to save, preserve”). More at bury.

ex.en: English words are often borrowed by other languages.
ex.ja: 英語の単語は他の言語にずいぶん取り入れられている。

ex.en: I will not borrow money from those people.
ex.ja: 私はあの連中からは金を借りない。

ex.en: Don't borrow more money than you can help.
ex.ja: 借りないですむ以上の金を借りるな。

en: Any building or complex of buildings in which a legislature meets.
Any citadel or complex of buildings similar to the Roman Capitol, particularly Italian and Roman citadels including temples to Jupiter, J…

capitol.ety: From Middle English Capitolie, via Anglo-Norman capitolie, Old French capitoile, from Latin Capitōlium (“Capitoline Hill, its temples; any similar citadel”), from the oblique stem of caput (“head”) + -ō (noun-forming suffix) or -ōlus (“-ole”, diminutive suffix) + -ium (toponym-forming suffix). Compare Latin capitō and capitulum. As a French magistrate, via French capitoul, from Capitole, the town hall of Toulouse. Doublet of Capitolium and capitoul.

en: Of or relating to the Celts.
Of the languages spoken by Celts.

Celtic.ety: Borrowed from French celtique or Latin celticus, equivalent to Celt + -ic. First attested in the 17th century.

ex.en: The museum has a fascinating collection of Celtic artifacts.
ex.ja: その博物館にはケルト時代の文化遺産のすばらしいコレクションがある。

ex.en: That museum has a superb collection of Celtic era cultural artifacts.
ex.ja: その博物館にはケルト時代の文化遺産のすばらしいコレクションがある。

en: The bottom of a face, (specifically) the typically jutting jawline below the mouth.
The ability to withstand being punched in the chin without being knocked out.
To perform a chin-up (exercise in which one lifts one's own weight while hanging from a bar).
To punch or hit (someone), especially on the chin (part of the body).

chin.ety:
From Middle English chyn, from Old English ċinn (“chin”), from Proto-West Germanic *kinnu, from Proto-Germanic *kinnuz (“chin”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵénus (“chin, jaw”).
Compare West Frisian/Dutch kin, Low German/German Kinn, Danish kind, Icelandic kinn, Welsh gen, Latin gena, Tocharian A śanweṃ, Ancient Greek γένυς (génus, “jaw”), Armenian ծնոտ (cnot), Persian چانه (čâne), Sanskrit हनु (hánu). Doublet of gena.

ex.en: How many chin-ups can you do, Tom?
ex.ja: トム、懸垂何回できる？

ex.en: I need to do something about this double chin.
ex.ja: この二重あごをなんとかしたいのよ。

ex.en: I hit him on the chin.
ex.ja: 彼のあごを殴ってやった。

en: Of, relating to, or belonging to a city, a citizen, or citizenship; municipal or civil.
Of or relating to the citizen, or of good citizenship and its rights and duties.

civic.ety: Borrowed from Latin cīvicus (“pertaining to a city or citizens”).

note.ja: ラテン語 civis（市民）から。civ + ic。→「市民の・市の」。

en: One who occupationally provides assistance by working with records, accounts, letters, etc.; an office worker.
A salesclerk; a person who serves customers in a store or market.
To act as a clerk, to perform the duties or functions of a clerk.
To assemble information about a patient during their initial assessment by actions such as a taking a detailed medical history and perfor…

clerk.ety:
From Middle English clerc, from Old English clerc, from Late Latin clēricus (“priest, clergyman, cleric”, also generally “learned man, clerk”), from Ancient Greek κληρικός (klērikós, “of the clergy”, adj. in church jargon), from κλῆρος (klêros, “lot, inheritance”, originally “shard used in casting lots”). Doublet of cleric.
Compare typologically Russian дьяк (dʹjak) (akin to дья́кон (dʹjákon)).

ex.en: Dr. Clark, may I ask a favor of you?
ex.ja: クラーク博士、お願いがあるのですが。

ex.en: He married his daughter to a bank clerk.
ex.ja: 彼は娘を銀行員にとつがせた。

ex.en: She is a clerk of the trading company.
ex.ja: 彼女は貿易会社の事務員です。

en: Significantly; to a degree worth considering.

considerably.ety:
Etymology tree
English considerable
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English considerably
From considerable + -ly.

ex.en: This area has been considerably built up of late.
ex.ja: この地区は最近家がかなり建て込んできた。

ex.en: Her health seems to have improved considerably of late.
ex.ja: 彼女は最近ずいぶん健康をとりもどしたようだ。

ex.en: The situation has improved considerably compared with what it was.
ex.ja: 以前と比べると状況は随分良くなった。

en: A small house.
A seasonal home of any size or stature, a recreational home or a home in a remote location.
To stay at a seasonal home, to go cottaging.
To have homosexual sex in a public lavatory; to practice cottaging.

cottage.ety:
Late Middle English, from Anglo-Norman cotage and Medieval Latin cotagium, from Old Northern French cot, cote (“cottage, hut”) + -age (“surrounding property”), from Old Norse kot, from Proto-Germanic *kutą, *kuta- (“shed”), probably of non-Indo-European origin, possibly borrowed from Proto-Finno-Ugric/Proto-Uralic *kota (“hut, tent”), probably akin to Proto-Iranian *kátah (“house; roof”). However, also compare Dutch and English hut.
Cognates
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Koate (“cottage, hut, small house”), Dutch kot (“ramshackle housing”), German Kate, Kote (“cot, cottage, hut”), Norwegian B

ex.en: There stands a cottage close to the forest.
ex.ja: 森の近くに一軒家がある。

ex.en: Tell me what cottage cheese is made from.
ex.ja: カッテージチーズは何からできてるか教えて。

ex.en: I saw a cottage in the distance.
ex.ja: 遠くに小屋が見えた。

en: To find fault (with something).
To evaluate (something), assessing its merits and faults.

criticize.ety: From critic + -ize; first element from Ancient Greek κριτικός (kritikós, “of or for judging, able to discern”), from κρίσις (krísis, “decision, judgement”).

ex.en: Nothing is as easy as to criticize others.
ex.ja: 他人を批判するほど易しいことはない。

ex.en: Anyone who criticizes him is asking for trouble.
ex.ja: あいつにケチをつけると後が怖い。

ex.en: I don't mind being criticized when I'm wrong.
ex.ja: 私は間違っている時に非難されても構わない。

en: In a natural, untreated state.
Characterized by simplicity, especially something not carefully or expertly made.
Any substance in its natural state.

crude.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *krewh₂-der.
Proto-Italic [Term?]
Latin crūdusbor.
Middle English crude
English crude
Doublet of crudo, which was borrowed from Italian, and (more distantly) raw through Proto-Indo-European.

ex.en: The method was crude, but very effective.
ex.ja: その方法は粗雑なものであったが、効果的だった。

ex.en: Crude oil has been falling in price.
ex.ja: 原油価格の値下がりが続いている。

ex.en: The crude oil price is falling further.
ex.ja: 原油価格の値下がりが続いている。

en: Any of the following symbols: ‒ (figure dash), – (en dash), — (em dash), or ― (horizontal bar).
A hyphen or minus sign.
To run quickly or for a short distance.
To leave or depart.
Damn!

dash.ety: From Middle English daschen, dassen, from Danish daske (“to slap, strike”), related to Swedish daska (“to smack, slap, spank”), of obscure origin. Compare German tatschen (“to grope, paw”), Old English dwǣsċan (“to quell, put out, destroy, extinguish”). See also dush.

ex.en: The man dashed the bottle against the wall.
ex.ja: 男はビンを壁に叩きつけた。

ex.en: A cat dashed out of the room.
ex.ja: 猫が部屋から飛び出した。

ex.en: He dashed to catch the last train.
ex.ja: 彼は最終列車に向かって全速力で急いだ。

en: The act of revealing something.
The making known of a previously hidden fact or series of facts to another party; the act of disclosing.

disclosure.ety: From disclose by analogy with closure. A purely English formation.

en: A disposition; an arrangement, categorization, or classification of things.
A kick or a handball of the ball during a game.

disposal.ety:
Etymology tree
French disposerbor.
English dispose
Proto-Indo-European *h₂el-

From dispose + -al.

ex.en: I have a lot of money at my disposal.
ex.ja: 私は自由に使えるお金がたくさんある。

ex.en: This is the money at your disposal.
ex.ja: これはあなたが自由にしてよいお金です。

ex.en: I left the money at his disposal.
ex.ja: 私はその金を彼の自由に任せた。

en: Distinguishing, used to or enabling the distinguishing of some thing.
Characteristic, typical.
A distinctive thing: a quality or property permitting distinguishing; a characteristic.
A distinctive accent.

distinctive.ety: From Latin distinctus, perfect passive participle of distinguere (to push apart, to divide; see distinct) + -ive (forming adjectives signifying relation or tendency to). Cognate with French distinctif and Medieval Latin distinctivus.

ex.en: Tom has a distinctive scar under his right eye.
ex.ja: トムは右目の下に独特の傷がある。

ex.en: Japan has many distinctive traits.
ex.ja: 日本には多くのはっきりとした特色がある。

ex.en: When mosquitoes beat their wings up and down, they produce a distinctive buzzing sound.
ex.ja: 蚊が羽を上下にバタバタすると、ブーンという独特の音がする。

zh: 無人航空載具 /无人航空载具

en: A male hymenopteran (ant, bee, hornet, or wasp), whose sole primary function is to mate with the queen.
One who performs menial or tedious work.
To kill or destroy with a drone (unmanned aircraft), or with a missile fired by a drone.

drone.ety:
From Middle English drane, dron, drone, from Old English drān, drǣn, from Proto-West Germanic *drānu, from Proto-Germanic *drenô, *drēnuz (“drone”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰreh₁n- (“bee, drone, hornet”).
Cognates
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Droane (“drone”), Dutch dar (“drone”), German Drohne (“drone”), Limburgish dreen, Droon (“drone”), Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nynorsk drone (“drone”), Swedish drönare (“drone”); also Belarusian тру́цень (trúcjenʹ, “drone”), Bulgarian търтей (tărtej, “drone”), Czech trubec (“drone”), Macedonian трут (trut, “drone”), Polish trąd, trut, tru

ex.en: She droned on for hours about her family history.
ex.ja: 彼女は数時間も彼女の家の歴史の話をくどくどしゃべった。

ex.en: Well, unmanned drones likely lack style, right.
ex.ja: 無人機じゃ味気ないだろ。

ex.en: I want to buy a drone, but my parents won't let me.
ex.ja: ドローンを買いたいんだけど親が買わせてくれない。

en: A group of people or vehicles, generally armed, who go with a person or people of importance to safeguard them on a journey or mission.
An accompanying person in such a group.
To attend to in order to guard and protect; to accompany as a safeguard (for the person escorted or for others); to give honorable or cer…
To accompany (a person) in order to compel them to go somewhere (e.g. to leave a building).

escort.ety: Borrowed from French escorte, itself borrowed from Italian scorta.

ex.en: I will serve you as an escort.
ex.ja: 私が送って差し上げましょう。

ex.en: May I escort you home?
ex.ja: お宅までお送りしましょうか？

ex.en: The security guards escorted Tom out of the building.
ex.ja: 警備員はトムをビルの外に放り出した。

en: In a firm or definite or strong manner.
Securely.

firmly.ety: From Middle English fermely; equivalent to firm + -ly.

ex.en: The event has fixed firmly in my mind.
ex.ja: その出来事がしっかりと私の心に取りついてしまった。

ex.en: I firmly believe that your time will come.
ex.ja: 私はあなたの番が来ると確信しているよ。

ex.en: He held on firmly to the branch.
ex.ja: 彼はしっかりと枝につかまった。

en: Powder obtained by grinding or milling cereal grains, especially wheat, or other foodstuffs such as soybeans and potatoes, and used to ba…
The food made by grinding and bolting cleaned wheat (not durum or red durum) until it meets specified levels of fineness, dryness, and fr…
To apply flour to something; to cover with flour.
To reduce to flour.

flour.ety:
Spelled (until about 1830) and meaning flower in the sense of flour being the "finest portion of ground grain" (compare French fleur de farine, fine fleur). Doublet of fleur, flor, and flower. Partially displaced native meal.
The U.S. standard of identity comes from 21CFR137.105.

ex.en: This cake contains flour, milk, eggs and sugar.
ex.ja: このケーキには小麦粉、牛乳、卵、砂糖が含まれています。

ex.en: He bought a lot of flour and oil.
ex.ja: 彼はたくさんの小麦粉と油を買い込んだ。

ex.en: That flour mill is now operated as a museum.
ex.ja: その製粉場は現在博物館として運営されている。

en: Of, or relating to Hinduism, or to Hindus and their culture.
A person adhering to the Hindu religion (Hinduism).

Hindu.ety: Derived from Classical Persian هِنْدُو (hindū, “Indian, Hindu”), from Middle Persian hndwk' (Hindūg, “Indian”), from hnd (Hind, “India”), from Old Persian 𐏃𐎡𐎯𐎢 (hiⁿdu-, “India”), from Sanskrit सिन्धु (síndhu, “river, stream; Indus”), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *síndʰuṣ, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *síndʰuš (“river”).

ex.en: The concept of zero comes from Hindu culture.
ex.ja: ゼロという概念は、ヒンドゥー文化に由来している。

ex.en: The concept of zero sprang from the Hindu culture.
ex.ja: ゼロという概念はヒンドゥー文化に由来している。

ex.en: Hindus do not eat beef.
ex.ja: ヒンズー教徒は牛肉を食べません。

en: Not direct
Not of obvious or immediate cause, but as a secondary result.
An indirect cost.
An indirect radiator.
To access by means of indirection; to dereference.

indirect.ety: From Middle French indirect, from Late Latin indirectus (“not direct”).

ex.en: Taxes consist of direct taxes and indirect ones.
ex.ja: 税は直接税と間接税からなっている。

ex.en: Consumption and alcohol taxes are indirect and are paid together with the cost.
ex.ja: 消費税、 酒税などは間接税で、代金と一緒に支払われる。

ex.en: New indirect taxes were imposed on spirits.
ex.ja: 新たな間接税が強い酒類に対して課せられた。

en: transitional
temporary
A transitional or temporary period between other events.

ex.en: Tom has been named interim head coach.
ex.ja: トムは臨時ヘッドコーチに指名された。

ex.en: It was only supposed to be an interim solution.
ex.ja: それはただの臨時の解決策だった。

en: A sudden, often uncontrolled movement, especially of the human body.
A quick pull on something.
To make a sudden uncontrolled movement.
To give a quick, often unpleasant tug or shake.

jerk.ety: Probably from Middle English yerk (“sudden motion”) and Middle English yerkid (“tightly pulled”), from Old English ġearc (“ready, active, quick”) and Old English ġearcian (“to prepare, make ready, procure, furnish, supply”). Cognate with Scots yerk (“to jerk”). Related also to English yare (“ready”).

ex.en: Suppose there's some jerk you just can't get on with.
ex.ja: 自分と気があわない、いけ好かない、人がいるとします。

ex.en: My boss is a jerk.
ex.ja: 私のボスは最低なやつだ。

ex.en: The train jerked forward.
ex.ja: 電車は急に発進した。

en: The state of being kind.
An instance of kind or charitable behaviour.

kindness.ety: From Middle English kyndenesse, equivalent to kind + -ness.

ex.en: She is a model of kindness for me.
ex.ja: 彼女の優しさは私にとって良い手本だ。

ex.en: We are grateful to you for your kindness.
ex.ja: 私たちはあなたのご親切に感謝しています。

ex.en: I am grateful to you for your kindness.
ex.ja: ご親切を感謝しています。

en: A scheme for the distribution of prizes by lot or chance, especially a gaming scheme in which one or more tickets bearing particular numb…
Something decided by chance.

lottery.ety: Borrowed from Italian lotteria, from the same root as Old English hlot (cognate with English lot). Compare French loterie (from Middle Dutch loterie). By surface analysis, lot + -ery.

ex.en: He won the first prize in the lottery.
ex.ja: 彼はくじ引きで一等賞を当てたよ。

ex.en: What would you do if you won the lottery?
ex.ja: 宝くじに勝ったらどうしますか。

ex.en: Mary had a dream that she won the lottery.
ex.ja: メアリーは宝くじに当たる夢を見た。

en: The absolute or relative size, extent or importance of something.
An order of magnitude.

ex.en: I hadn't realized the magnitude of the problems.
ex.ja: 私はその問題の重要さがわかっていなかった。

ex.en: He realized the magnitude of his crime.
ex.ja: 彼は犯した罪の大きさを悟った。

ex.en: I've never seen a pearl of such magnitude!
ex.ja: こんなに大きな真珠は見たことがない。

en: Made less or reduced by (followed by an expression of number or quantity).
Without; deprived of.
The minus sign (−).
A negative quantity.
Being a negative quantity; pertaining to a deficit or reduction.
That is below zero by (a specified amount) on a scale.
To subtract.

minus.ety: From Middle English mynus, from Latin minus, neuter form of minor, comparative form of parvus (“small, little”), from the Proto-Indo-European root *mey- (“few, small”).

ex.en: How many is nine minus six?
ex.ja: 九引く六はいくつですか。

ex.en: The thermometer registered minus ten last night.
ex.ja: 昨夜、温度計はマイナス１０度を示した。

ex.en: The temperature went down to minus ten degrees centigrade last night.
ex.ja: 昨夜は-10℃まで冷え込んだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 minus（より少なく）から。min（小さい）。→「マイナス・〜を引いた」。

en: Without clothing or other covering of the skin; without clothing on the genitals or female nipples.
Of a color (such as beige or tan) that evokes bare flesh.
A painting, sculpture, photograph or other artwork or mass-media-reproduced image depicting one or more human figure(s) in a state of nea…
The state of total nudity.

nude.ety: Entered English 1493 as a legal term, meaning "unsupported, not formally attested," from Middle English nud, from Latin nūdus (“naked, bare”).

ex.en: The children were swimming in the nude.
ex.ja: 子供たちは裸で泳いでいた。

ex.en: What's wrong with being nude in your own house?
ex.ja: 家の中で全裸で何が悪い！

ex.en: Where are the three nude statues in the exhibition?
ex.ja: 展覧会に出ている３つの裸像がどこですか？

en: A vent or similar passage to allow the escape of something.
Something which allows for the release of one's desires.

outlet.ety: From Middle English outlete, outeleate, ut-lete, derived from Middle English outleten (“to allow, let out, emit”), equivalent to out- + let. Compare West Frisian útlit (“outlet”), Dutch uitlaat (“outlet”), German Auslass (“outlet”).

ex.en: Playing baseball is an outlet for energy.
ex.ja: 野球は精力のはけ口になる。

ex.en: Gary found an outlet for his energy in playing football.
ex.ja: ゲーリーはフットボールをする事に活力のはけ口を見つけた。

ex.en: Where can I find an outlet for all my anger?
ex.ja: この遣り場なき怒りをどこにぶつければいいのか。

en: A value kept constant during an experiment, equation, calculation, or similar, but varied over other versions of the experiment, equation…
A variable that describes a property or characteristic of some system (material, object, event, etc.) or some aspect thereof.

parameter.ety: From French paramètre, from New Latin parametrum (“parameter”), from Ancient Greek παρα- (para-, “beside”) + μέτρον (métron, “measure”).

note.ja: para（そばに）+ meter（測る）。補助として測るもの →「媒介変数・条件・範囲」。

en: To take a temporary rest, take a break for a short period after an effort.
To stop (an activity) for a while.
A temporary stop or rest; an intermission of action; interruption; suspension; cessation.
A short time for relaxing and doing something else.

pause.ety: From Middle French pause, from Latin pausa, from Ancient Greek παῦσις (paûsis), from Ancient Greek παύω (paúō, “stop”), of uncertain origin. Doublet of pausa.

ex.en: He spoke for ten minutes without a pause.
ex.ja: 彼は息もつかず１０分間話し続けた。

ex.en: The speaker paused and then went on talking again.
ex.ja: 講師は一息入れてから、また話し続けた。

ex.en: Tom paused and took a deep breath.
ex.ja: トムは止まって、深呼吸をした。

en: To make a solemn promise (to do something).
To deposit something as a security; to pawn.
A solemn promise to do something.
A promise to abstain from drinking alcohol.

pledge.ety: From Middle English plege, from Anglo-Norman plege, from Old French plege (Modern French pleige) from Medieval Latin plevium, plebium, from plebiō (“to pledge”), from Frankish *plehan (“to pledge; to support; to guarantee”). Akin to Old High German pflegan (“to take care of, be accustomed to”), Old Saxon plegan (“to vouch for”), Old English plēon (“to risk, endanger”). More at plight.

ex.en: She pledged herself never to do it again.
ex.ja: 彼女は二度とそんなことをしないと誓った。

ex.en: He pledged to marry me when he returned home.
ex.ja: 彼は帰国したら私と結婚すると誓った。

ex.en: I give my pledge that I will quit smoking.
ex.ja: たばこはやめると誓います。

en: An entrance, entry point, or means of entry.
A large primary adit as the main entrance to a mine.
Of or relating to a porta, especially the porta of the liver.
To use a portal (magical or technological doorway).

portal.ety: From Middle English portal, porttol, from Old French portal and Medieval Latin portāle, from porta.

ex.en: What do you need to build a nether portal?
ex.ja: ネザーポータルを構築するには何が必要ですか？

note.ja: ラテン語 porta（門）から。→「（立派な）入口・玄関・ポータルサイト」。port（港）と同じ祖先。

en: A written order from an authorized medical practitioner for provision of a medicine or other treatment, such as (ophthalmology) the speci…
The medicine or treatment provided by such an order.

prescription.ety: Borrowed from Middle French, from Old French prescripcion, from Latin praescriptio (“preface; pretext; something written ahead of time”), from prae- (“pre-, before”) + scribere (“to write”) + -tio (“-tion, forming nouns”). Equivalent to prescribe + -tion.

ex.en: Go to the doctor to get your prescription!
ex.ja: 処方箋をもらうために医者に行きなさい。

ex.en: To get a prescription, go to a doctor.
ex.ja: 処方箋をもらうために医者に行きなさい。

ex.en: You cannot purchase this medicine without a prescription.
ex.ja: その薬は処方箋無しで買ってはいけません。

note.ja: pre（前に）+ script（書く）+ ion。前もって書いて指示したもの →「処方箋・規定」。prescribe（処方する）。

One who protests a bill of exchange, or note.

A young rat.
To bring forth whelps or give birth to pups.

A style or process of recruiting.
A nonmetallic element (symbol Si) with an atomic number of 14 and atomic weight of 28.0855.

To cut into slices.

Having the properties of a slice knot.

A jab given with the spurs.

To urge or encourage to action, or to a more vigorous pursuit of an object

spur.ety: From Middle English spure, spore, from Old English spora, spura, from Proto-West Germanic *spurō, from Proto-Germanic *spurô, from Proto-Indo-European *sperH- (“to kick”).

To use a telegraph; to send a message by telegraph.
To clearly communicate to another nonverbally (whether by gesture, a change in attitude, or any other sign), and especially unintentionally.

telegraph.ety: Borrowed from French télégraphe, equivalent to tele- (“far, distant”) + -graph (“writing”), suggested as a new name for Claude Chappe's overland semaphore network by André François Miot de Mélito in place of Chappe's original tachygraphe (“tachygraph, fast writer”).

ex.en: My parents telegraphed me to come back at once.
ex.ja: 両親からすぐに帰れと電報が来た。

ex.ja: 彼らは万事異状なしということを電報で伝えた。

ex.ja: 事務局は私の願書を受け取っていないと電報で知らせてきた。

en: Of, pertaining to, caused by, or characteristic of cowpox.
Of or pertaining to cowpox as a source of material for vaccination against smallpox; also, of or pertaining to such material used for vac…
A substance given to stimulate a body's production of antibodies and provide immunity against a disease without causing the disease itsel…
The process of vaccination; immunization, inoculation.

vaccine.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin vaccīnus (“of or derived from a cow”), from vacca (“cow (female cattle)”) + -īnus (suffix meaning ‘of or pertaining to’ forming adjectives). Sense 1 refers to the early use of the cowpox virus as a vaccination against smallpox: see New Latin variolae vaccīnae (“cowpox”, plural, literally “infectious diseases of cattle causing pustules”), coined by the British physician and scientist Edward Jenner (1749–1823).

To adopt; to receive into a family as one's offspring
to bring or receive into close connection; to ally.

ex.ja: その納屋は小さかったが頑丈だった。

clause.ety: From Middle English clause, claus, borrowed from Old French clause, from Medieval Latin clausa (Latin diminutive clausula (“close, end; a clause, close of a period”)), from Latin clausus, past participle of claudere (“to shut, close”). See close, its doublet.

A group of galaxies, nebulae, or stars that appear to the naked eye to be near each other.
To collect (animals, people, objects, data points, etc) into clusters (noun sense 1).
To cover (with clusters); to scatter or strew in clusters (within); to distribute (objects) within such that they form clusters.

cluster.ety:

A solid figure bounded by a cylinder and two parallel planes intersecting the cylinder.
To calender; to press (paper, etc.) between rollers to make it glossy.

cylinder.ety: From Middle French chilindre, cylindre, from Latin cylindrus, from Ancient Greek κύλινδρος (kúlindros), from κυλίνδω (kulíndō) "I roll or wallow" (intransitive). Doublet of calander and calender.

ex.en: The gas was compressed into a gas cylinder.

A stripper.

dancer.ety: From Middle English dauncer, dawncere, dancere, equivalent to dance + -er.

ex.ja: つまり彼女は下手な踊り子だ。

Unwilling to listen or be persuaded; determinedly inattentive.

deaf.ety:

To reduce (wages); to deduct from (someone).

ex.ja: 彼が恋をしているのは明らかだ。

ex.ja: 地球が丸いということは今では明らかである。

An important or long journey, for example a march or a voyage.

ex.en: He was sent to jail for the robbery.

ex.en: Bank robbery will cost you ten years in prison.
ex.ja: 銀行強盗すると懲役１０年食らうぞ。

en: An act of rubbing.
A difficulty or problem.
To move (one object) while maintaining contact with another object over some area, with pressure and friction.
To be rubbed against something.

rub.ety:
Inherited from Middle English rubben, of unknown origin; possibly ultimately from Proto-Germanic *rubbōną, a hypothetical variant of *ruppōną (“to tear (off), rip; to wear away, rub”), related to *reufaną (“to tear”) (> English reave). If so, a doublet of rip.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian rubje (“to rub, scrape”), German Low German rubben (“to rub”), Low German rubblig (“rough, uneven”), Dutch robben, rubben (“to rub smooth; scrape; scrub”), Danish rubbe (“to rub, scrub”), Icelandic and Norwegian rubba (“to scrape”).
More at reave.
Compare typologically Latin fricō < friō < Proto-Indo-Europe

ex.en: Everything he says rubs me the wrong way.
ex.ja: 彼の言うことすべてが、私の神経を逆なでするのです。

ex.en: I sure rubbed your nose in shit.
ex.ja: お前の鼻をクソに擦りつけてやった。

ex.en: Never rub your eyes with dirty hands.
ex.ja: 汚れた手で目をこすってはいけません。

en: A willow.
Any tree that resembles a willow.
To make a sudden attack (e.g. on an enemy from a defended position).
To set out on an excursion; venture; depart (often followed by "forth").

sally.ety: From Middle English saly, from Old English saliġ, sealh (“willow”). More at sallow.

ex.en: Sally and I work in the same office.
ex.ja: サリーは職場の仲間です。

ex.en: Sally gave me a good piece of information.
ex.ja: サリーは私に良い情報を１つ教えてくれた。

ex.en: Sally made her brother clean the bathroom.
ex.ja: サリーは弟にバスルームを掃除させた。

en: Dispersed, spread apart into disunited units.
Seemingly randomly distributed.

ex.en: Broken glass lay scattered all over the road.
ex.ja: ガラスの破片が、道路一面に散らばってたよ。

ex.en: The sudden noise scattered the birds.
ex.ja: 突然の物音に鳥たちは散り散りに飛び去った。

ex.en: The wind scattered the leaves about.
ex.ja: 風が葉を吹き散らした。

en: A person sent out to gather and bring back information; especially, one employed in war to gain information about the enemy and ground.
An act of scouting or reconnoitering.
To explore a wide terrain, as if on a search.
To observe, watch, or look for, as a scout; to follow for the purpose of observation, as a scout.

ex.en: When did you become a Boy Scout?
ex.ja: ボーイスカウトになったのはいつぐらい？

ex.ja: ボーイスカウトたちは自分たちの作った物を一軒一軒売ってまわった。

ex.en: I was scouted by a model agency while walking around Shibuya.
ex.ja: 渋谷を歩いていてモデルエージェンシーにスカウトされた。

Sexual activity; concern with, or interest in, sexual activity.

en: A blow, especially one given with the open hand, or with something broad and flat.
A sharp percussive sound like that produced by such a blow.
To strike someone, typically with an open hand, often on the face.
To cause something to strike soundly.
Exactly, precisely

slap.ety: From Middle English slappen, of uncertain origin, possibly imitative. Compare Low German Slappe (“slap”), whence also German Schlappe (“defeat”). Compare also Italian sleppa (“slap”).

ex.en: Slapped in the face, I didn't fight back.
ex.ja: 顔に平手打ちされたけれども、私は抵抗しなかった。

ex.en: Even so ... she didn't have to slap me!
ex.ja: だからって・・・なにもひっぱたくことないじゃないか。

ex.en: Can I slap you? I can't contain myself.
ex.ja: 引っ叩いていい？腹の虫が治まらないんだけど。

en: Beefsteak: a slice of beef, broiled or cut for broiling.
A relatively large, thick slice or slab cut from another animal, a vegetable, etc.
To cook (something, especially fish) like or as a steak.

steak.ety:
From Middle English steike, from Old Norse steik (“roast; meat roasted on a stick”). The verb is either from the noun or from steikja (“to roast”).
The modern pronunciation shows an irregular change of Early Modern English /ɛː/ to /eɪ/ in the standard language; contrast this with the development of other words such as speak and wreak.

ex.en: He ate up the steak and ordered another.
ex.ja: 彼はそのステーキを平らげてもう１つ注文した。

ex.en: Would you like to have steak for dinner?
ex.ja: 夜ご飯にステーキはどうですか？

ex.en: Steak and red wine make a good combination.
ex.ja: ステーキと赤ワインはいい取り合わせだ。

en: An act of following in sequence.
A sequence of things in order.

succession.ety: Inherited from Middle English [Term?], from Old French succession, from Latin successiō (noun).

ex.en: They won the Japan Cup three years in succession.
ex.ja: 彼らは３年連続してジャパン・カップに優勝した。

ex.en: After a succession of warm days, the weather became cold.
ex.ja: 暖かい日が連続した後、天候は寒くなった。

ex.en: He came to the throne by succession.
ex.ja: 彼は世襲によって王位についた。

note.ja: suc（次に）+ cess（進む）+ ion。次々に続くこと →「連続・継承」。

en: A person who is authorized to supervise, direct or administer something.
A police officer rank, positioned above chief inspector, and below chief superintendent.
Overseeing; superintending.

superintendent.ety: From Ecclesiastical Latin superintendens, a calque of Ancient Greek ἐπίσκοπος (epískopos); thence being distantly related to English bishop.

en: The act of suspecting something or someone, especially of something wrong.
The condition of being suspected.

suspicion.ety: From Middle English suspecioun, borrowed from Latin suspīciō, suspīciōnem, from suspicere, from sub- (“up to”) with specere (“to look at”). Perhaps partly through the influence of Old French sospeçon (or rather the Anglo-Norman form suspecioun). Equivalent to suspect + -ion.

ex.en: He fell under the suspicion of the police.
ex.ja: 彼は警察の嫌疑を受けた。

ex.en: Her unusual behavior gave rise to our suspicions.
ex.ja: 彼女の異常な行動が私たちの疑いを引き起こした。

ex.en: I have a suspicion about his death.
ex.ja: 私は彼の死に対して疑いを持っている。

en: To clean (a surface) by means of a stroking motion of a broom or brush.
To move through a (horizontal) arc or similar long stroke.
A single action of sweeping.
The person who steers a dragon boat.

sweep.ety: From Middle English swepen, from Proto-West Germanic *swaipijan (unattested in Old English), from Proto-Germanic *swaipijaną. Cognate with Early Modern West Frisian swiepe (“whip, cleanse, sweep”), from Old Frisian swēpa, suepa (“sweep”). More distantly related to Old Norse sveipa (whence Swedish svepa). See also swoop.

ex.en: Did you order the room to be swept?
ex.ja: 部屋を掃除するように命じましたか。

ex.en: A shadow of anxiety swept across her face.
ex.ja: 不安の影が彼女の顔をさっとよぎった。

ex.en: The children were assigned to sweep the room.
ex.ja: 子供たちは部屋の掃除を割り当てられた。

A psychotherapist specifically.

en: After that time, from then on; thenceforth.
After that (the thing aforementioned).
Synonym of hereafter (“future existence or state”).
Synonym of hereafter (“existence after death”).

thereafter.ety: From Middle English therafter, theraftir, þerefter, þerafter, þeræfter, from Old English þǣræfter (“after that; thereafter”), equivalent to there + after. Cognate with Saterland Frisian deerätter (“thereafter”), West Frisian dêrefter (“behind that; thereafter”), Dutch daarachter (“behind that; thereafter”), German Low German daarachter (“behind that”), Danish derefter (“thereafter”), Swedish därefter (“thereafter”).

ex.en: Thereafter we heard no more from him.
ex.ja: その後彼からは便りが無かった。

ex.en: Thereafter, he was gradually promoted until he became company president.
ex.ja: 彼はその後、累進して社長にまで進んだ。

en: Painstaking and careful not to miss or omit any detail.
Utter; complete; absolute.

thorough.ety: From Middle English thoruȝ, þoruȝ, from Old English þuruh, a byform of Old English þurh, whence comes English through. The adjective derives from the preposition and adverb. The word developed a syllabic form in cases where the word was fully stressed: when it was used as an adverb, adjective, or noun, and less commonly when used as a preposition.

ex.en: He made a thorough analysis of the problem.
ex.ja: 彼はその問題を徹底的に分析した。

ex.en: The theory is based on thorough research.
ex.ja: その理論は周到な研究に基づいている。

ex.en: A thorough investigation is now in progress.
ex.ja: 詳しい調査は今進行中です。

en: The training or instruction provided by a teacher or tutor.
Paid private classes taken outside of formal education; tutoring. (also used attributively)

tuition.ety: From Anglo-Norman tuycioun, from Old French tuicion, from Latin tuitiō (“guard, protection, defense”), from tuēri (“to watch, guard, see, observe”). Compare intuition, tutor.

ex.en: I got a grant for my tuition.
ex.ja: 奨学金が交付された。

ex.en: I am working to save for my college tuition.
ex.ja: 大学の授業料をためるために働いています。

ex.en: They announced an increase in tuition fees.
ex.ja: 学校は授業料の値上げを発表した。

en: An abnormal growth; differential diagnosis includes abscess, metaplasia, and neoplasia.

tumor.ety: From Middle English tumour, from Old French tumour, from Latin tumor (“swelling”), from tumeō (“bulge, swell”, verb), from Proto-Italic *tumēō, from Proto-Indo-European *tewh₂- (“to swell”). Related to English thumb.

ex.en: Tom had a brain tumor.
ex.ja: トムには脳腫瘍があった。

ex.en: I got a stomach tumor and had to have it operated on.
ex.ja: 胃に腫瘍ができたので切ってもらった。

ex.en: I have a tumor.
ex.ja: 私、腫瘍があるんだ。

en: The sale of products, often in large quantities, to retailers or other merchants.
Of or relating to sale in large quantities, for resale.
Extensive, indiscriminate, all-encompassing; blanket.
In bulk or large quantity.
Indiscriminately.
To sell at wholesale.

ex.en: Wholesale prices are basically flat.
ex.ja: 卸売物価は基本的に安定している。

ex.en: A retail merchant buys wholesale and sells retail.
ex.ja: 小売商人は卸しで仕入れて小売りで売る。

ex.en: This morning, Mr Yamaha bought 30 kilos of walnuts wholesale.
ex.ja: 今朝、山羽さんが卸で胡桃を３０キロ買いました。

en: To apportion out, distribute.
To manage or supervise the conduct, performance or execution of; to govern or regulate the parameters for the conduct, performance or exe…

administer.ety: From Middle English administren, from Old French aminister, from Latin administrare (“to manage, execute”), from ad (“to”) + ministrare (“to attend, serve”), from minister (“servant”); see minister.

ex.en: The mayor administers the affairs of the city.
ex.ja: 市長は市政を司る。

ex.en: The Secretary of State administers foreign affairs.
ex.ja: 国務長官は対外関係を統括する。

ex.en: The doctor administered medicine to the patient.
ex.ja: 医者は患者に投薬した。

en: Large projectile weapons, in modern usage usually large guns, but also rocket artillery.
An army unit that uses such weapons, or a military formation using projectile weapons, such as archers.

artillery.ety: From Middle English artillerie, from Old French artillerie (“collection of military engines, crossbows, lances etc.”), from artillier (“to equip, provide with contraptions”), alteration of atiller (“to arrange, adjust, put on clothes or, especially, pieces of armour”) (influenced by art), itself from Vulgar Latin *apticlō < **apticulō, from Latin aptō (“to make capable”).
